comments.text: 6510 processor port: init_game clears bit 0 (BASIC ROM out, $36); music_read sets 0 (all RAM) for one read of the tune under the KERNAL and puts the old value back.

Scratch byte with many users: the fire flag from read_joystick (1 = held), the low byte of a speech sample's end address, place_sprite's X bit 8 flag, a divisor or multiplier, a loop index in build_3d_view.
High byte of the current speech sample's end address (play_speech).

Scratch pointer/bytes $AC/$AD: roadblock cell address (place_roadblock, clear_roadblock), police object index in police_ai, place_sprite's Y, colour RAM pointer in clear_screen, distance sums in mayday_distance.
High byte of the $AC pointer; also the window X offset (low) in objects_to_sprites.

Scratch pointer $AE/$AF: map cell pointer (car_cell_update, roadblock_check, build_3d_view), damage gauge cell, screen pointer in draw_cockpit and clear_screen; $AE alone is place_sprite's shape pointer and the dividend shift byte in divide_16_8.
High byte of the $AE pointer; place_sprite's X low byte.
Map address of the cell under the car ($C9 low, $CA high), kept by car_cell_update and read by roadblock_check.
High byte of car_cell_ptr.
May Day's spiral limit, from the landing table ($4FE0): when her circling radius $69F9 reaches it she starts to home on the landing point.

Note stream pointer of the voice being stepped ($D9 low, $DA high; music_step_voices, music_voice_note). On the instruction page $D9 is instead the stepping colour of the PRESS FIRE TO START line (title_page, draw_title_text).
High byte of music_ptr.
May Day's X minus $88 (16 bits, $EA/$EB), for mayday_distance.
High byte of mayday_ref_x.
May Day's Y minus $32 (16 bits, $EC/$ED), for mayday_distance.
High byte of mayday_ref_y.
Scratch pointer $FB/$FC: speech sample pointer, telex source line, map view base in build_3d_view, sprite bit mask in place_sprite, police cell address in police_ai.
High byte of the $FB pointer; also a column index in build_3d_view.
Stick up/down from read_joystick ($FF up, 1 down, 0); also scratch: speech length, telex destination pointer ($FD/$FE), divide_16_8's quotient, multiply_8_8's low byte.
Stick left/right from read_joystick ($FF left, 1 right, 0); also scratch: divide_16_8's remainder, multiply_8_8's high byte.

Sound choice on the instruction page: 1 THEME TUNE ONLY, 2 SOUND EFFECTS ONLY, 3 BOTH (set to 3 by part_entry). Bit 0 enables the music in irq_sound; bit 1 the crash, gun and roadblock effects, which test it themselves. The locator beep that bit 1 would also cover never plays (irq_sound).
Non-zero once the altimeter reads below 060 (altimeter_tick); hit_sprite accepts the car touching May Day as a catch only then. Cleared by init_game.
The map cell build_3d_view looks from ($02FA high, $02FB low); written every rebuild, read by nothing found.
Low byte of view_cell (build_3d_view's view point), never read.
Police sprites (bits 0-2) the bullet has hit, stored by hit_sprite; police_ai sends such a car to police_shot and clears the byte ($4D7C).

Police sprites (bits 0-2) that touched the car or each other, stored by hit_sprite and car_hits_police and never cleared: police_ai holds a car named here still, resetting its countdown to $20 on every pass, until a later collision replaces the set.
0 while May Day circles, 1 once her radius has reached the spiral limit and she heads for the landing point (mayday_update). Cleared by init_game.

Set to $98 by title_page and mission_complete; cleared by part_entry, by init_game and by game_start once the chase is set up. While it is set, game_irq ignores every interrupt but the raster one, and car_move_tick does nothing.
Base of init_game's copy of the variable templates: $8300+Y to $0300+Y for Y = $34-$FF, so $0334-$03FF start every chase from the values at $8334-$83FF.
Low byte of the BASIC tokeniser vector ($0304/$0305); part_entry writes $D0 here, the low byte it also gives the BRK and NMI vectors. Nothing in the part uses BASIC, so the purpose is unknown.

How the chase ended: 0 while it runs; $80 caught May Day (hit_sprite); $40 the altimeter reached 000 (altimeter_tick); $27 or 47 the damage gauge is full (car_crash at 40 points, add_damage at 47). Read by world_update and speak_result.

KERNAL IRQ vector: the KERNAL's $EA31 at the hand-over, game_irq ($5026) from install_game_irq on. Nothing sets it back: the instruction and success pages run with interrupts off instead (title_page switches CIA 1's interrupts off, and the stubs before them SEI).
High byte of the IRQ vector.
KERNAL BRK vector, set to restart_to_menu ($43D0) by part_entry.
High byte of the BRK vector.
KERNAL NMI vector, set to restart_to_menu ($43D0) by part_entry: the RESTORE key goes back to the instruction page.
High byte of the NMI vector.
Last coarse scroll step in X: 1, 0 or $FF (map_coarse_step); build_3d_view and car_cell_update adjust by it.
Last coarse scroll step in Y: 1, 0 or $FF (map_coarse_step).
Set by map_coarse_step when the map has moved a cell; build_3d_view rebuilds the 3D view and clears it.
Set by build_3d_view when its buffer holds a new picture; copy_3d_view copies it in the IRQ and clears it.
The car's world X in pixels (16 bits, $0338/$0339; $0190 at the start), stepped by 2 by scroll_map.
High byte of car_world_x.
The car's world Y in pixels (16 bits, $033A/$033B; $01BC at the start).
High byte of car_world_y.
Map address of the top-left cell of the 13 x 40 map window on screen ($033C/$033D; $AF35 at the start).
High byte of map_window.
The map band's X fine scroll, 0-6 in steps of 2 (scroll_map; written to $D016 by raster_map_band).
The map band's Y fine scroll, 1-7 in steps of 2 (scroll_map; written to $D011 by raster_map_band).
The car's speed as a delay, 1 (fastest) to $3F (starts at $3F): car_move_tick waits delay/4+1 frames between 2-pixel moves. Changed by speed_and_fire, raised by car_crash, shown by draw_speed_gauge.
Cleared by scroll_map on every move; nothing found reads it.
car_move_tick's frame countdown to the next 2-pixel move.
main_loop's pass counter: every 16th pass runs speed_and_fire.
main_loop's second counter: every other speed pass also steers.
Set by car_crash; while non-zero read_joystick returns no direction and no fire and further crashes are ignored. Cleared by scroll_map when the car next moves, and by title_page.
The heading of the car's last move (car_move_tick); car_crash puts the heading back to it.
locator_beep's countdown to the next beep.
Locator beep interval: the distance to May Day / 16, plus 1 (mayday_distance). Read only by locator_beep, which never runs.
How many more locator_beep calls the lamp stays purple (2 per beep).
mayday_update's pass countdown: 7 while circling, 8 while homing.
Coarse X step per heading for map_coarse_step: entries 0-7 forward, 8-15 reverse; 1 = one column right, $81 = one column left, 0 = none.
Coarse Y step per heading: $7E one map row down, $FE (negative, taken as -$7E) one row up, 0 none; 0-7 forward, 8-15 reverse.
Fine X direction per heading for scroll_map: 1 or $81 (bit 7 = the other way), 0 none; 0-7 forward, 8-15 reverse.
Fine Y direction per heading for scroll_map, same coding as step_fine_x.

The cockpit clock as eight characters less $64: hour tens and units ($0390, $0391), separator $0A, minute tens and units ($0393, $0394), separator, second tens and units ($0396, $0397); $0398 unused, $0399 the frame count (update_clock).
Clock hour units digit.
Clock minute tens digit.
Clock minute units digit.
Clock second tens digit.
Clock second units digit.
Frames 0-59 of the current clock second (update_clock); place_roadblock uses its low five bits as a random site.
The car's heading, 0-7: 0 up, then clockwise in 45-degree steps (steer_car).
Damage: +1 per crash (car_crash) or roadblock (add_damage). A crash that brings it to 40 ends the chase; a roadblock ends it only at 47. Shown by draw_damage_gauge.
Pursuit counter, raised by car_cell_update when the car enters a new block; police cars start once it reaches their threshold, and at 20 a roadblock appears and it drops to 18.
0 in forward gear, 8 in reverse; ORed into the heading as the index of the step tables.
scroll_map's flags: bit 0 a coarse X step is due, bit 1 a coarse Y step.
Sprite pointers of the map car for headings 0-7: $80-$87 (shapes at $2000-$21FF).
AND masks $FE, $FD ... $7F that clear one sprite's bit, indexed by sprite number.
Bit masks 1, 2, 4 ... $80, one per sprite.
Sprite pointers of May Day's parachute for drift directions 0-7: $90-$97 (shapes at $2400-$25FF).

Digitised speech (credited in the intro to David Aubrey-Jones), one bit per sample: interrupts off, SID volume 0, reads a 16-bit length at the sample address (LDA # operands at $1002 low and $1006 high, poked by the caller), then plays the bytes after it MSB first, each 1 bit setting the volume $D418 to $0F (speech_bit_on) and each 0 bit to 0 (speech_bit_off), so the click of the volume register is the sound. Stops at the address plus the length with volume 0 and returns with interrupts still off (a NOP at $1069 where a CLI could be). Samples: $1090 (length $194), $1225 ($6E4), $190A.
Operand of LDA #: the low byte of the speech sample's address, rewritten by speak_result and mission_complete before each call ($0A in the image, i.e. sample $190A).
Operand of LDA #: the high byte of the speech sample's address, rewritten with speech_addr_lo ($19 in the image).

play_speech continued: volume 0, the length word at the sample address is added to the address to give the end in $02/$03, then the bit loop ($1028) plays eight bits per byte until the pointer reaches the end.
A 1 bit of speech: SID volume $0F, then fifteen NOPs that make the bit as long as a 0 bit.
A 0 bit of speech: SID volume 0, then speech_delay, padding the bit to the length of a 1 bit.
Three NOPs and RTS: timing padding called once per bit by play_speech and inside speech_bit_off.
Speech sample: length word $0194, then 402 bytes of 1-bit sound (MSB first) to $1223. Played by speak_result when the damage gauge is full, before sample $190A. What it says is not established.
One byte between speech samples, not played.
Speech sample: length word $06E4, then 1762 bytes of 1-bit sound to $1908. Played at the start of the success telex (mission_complete).
Speech sample $1225 continued ($1600-$1908).
The byte after sample $1225 ends ($1908) and before sample $190A starts; not played.
Speech sample: length word $0699, then 1687 bytes of 1-bit sound to $1FA2. Played by speak_result after a lost chase (altimeter at 000, or after sample $1090).
Speech sample $190A continued ($1D00-$1FA2).
$1FA3-$1FFF after the last sample: bytes no routine reads (a remnant of a longer sample, or fill).
Sprite shapes $80-$87: the player's car seen from above in the eight headings (0 up, clockwise), sprite 7 on the map.
Sprite shapes $88-$8F: the police car in the eight headings (police_ai via $69A0).
Sprite shapes $90-$97: May Day under her parachute, one per drift direction (mayday_drift via $03E0).
Shapes $98-$9F ($2600-$27FF): $98 and $99 are scattered dots, $9A-$9F striped fill; no pointer found uses them.

Shapes $A0-$A3: the steering wheel's left and right halves, straight ($A0/$A1) and turned ($A2/$A3), sprites 4 and 5 in the cockpit; $A4-$A7 ($2900-$29FF) are near copies of them that nothing selects.
Shapes $A8-$AB ($2A00-$2AFF): striped fill, not used.
Shapes $AC-$AF: $AC the bullet (a single dot), $AD/$AE the two blink frames of a shot police car, $AF a third debris frame nothing selects.
$2C00-$2FFF (shapes $B0-$BF): striped fill like uninitialised RAM; not used.

Character set of the cockpit, the instruction page and the telex (selected at the bottom raster split and by title_page), glyphs $00-$7F: the dashboard and windscreen frame pieces the cockpit picture is built from ($04-$50), and the digits 0-9 and : at $64-$6E (clock, altimeter).

Cockpit character set, glyphs $80-$FF: the letters A-Z at $80-$99 and . , / ! - [ ] + at $9A-$A1 used by every page of text, more cockpit pieces at $A2-$A7, the 3D view pieces the strips use ($A8-$BB, $D0-$F4) and the damage gauge fills $C4-$CB.

Character set of the map band (selected by raster_map_band), glyphs $00-$7F, multicolour: the map uses $00-$4F and $FF (roofs and building blocks, road pieces, the junction markers $12-$19) plus the roadblock hatches $48/$49 placed in play; the glyphs above include an alphabet and digits the map does not use.
Map character set, glyphs $80-$FF: a byte-for-byte copy of glyphs $00-$7F ($3800-$3BFF).

Start-of-chase setup: clears the 32 roadblock sites (clear_roadblock), runs through 34 NOPs ($400B-$402C), stops timer A of CIA 1, sets the fine scroll start values $033E = 4 and $033F = 1, puts May Day's start ($01FA, $01FA) into object 0's template, volume 15, pick_landing_point, clears $02E1, $0313 and irq_lock $02FF, enables sprites 4 and 5 (the steering wheel, pointers $A0/$A1, white, at X $5E/$75, Y $75), copies the object templates $6800-$68FF to the live table $6900, sprite multicolours yellow/red, sprite 7 light blue, character set $3800, border blue, background dark grey, multicolour text, BASIC ROM out ($01 bit 0 cleared), patch_map, and the variable templates $8334-$83FF to $0334-$03FF.

Writes five bytes from $4152 (00 00 00 01 01) to map cells $9EEF-$9EF3 (row 24, columns 39-43) and five from $4157 (05 09 09 09 09) to $9FFC-$A000 (row 26, columns 56-60). In this image the first spot holds $4D $4F $4E $2A $01 at the hand-over, so four cells become road; the second already matches. Why they are rewritten is open.
patch_map's five cell values for map $9EEF-$9EF3 (row 24, columns 39-43): 00 00 00 01 01.
patch_map's five cell values for map $9FFC-$A000 (row 26, columns 56-60): 05 09 09 09 09.

The cockpit clock, once a frame from the IRQ: frames $0399 to 60, then seconds $0397/$0396, minutes $0394/$0393 and hours $0391/$0390, one decimal digit each, wrapping 24:00 to 00:00; writes the eight characters $0390-$0397 (digits and the separators at $0392/$0395, each plus $64) to screen $05A6-$05AD. Starts at 10:18:00 (template $8390); one clock second is 60 frames, 1.2 s on a PAL machine.

Positions and switches on one sprite: A = sprite number + 1, X = X low byte, Y = Y, carry = X bit 8, $AE = shape pointer. Builds the sprite's bit in $FB, stores the pointer at $07F7+A (screen $0400's pointer table) and the position at $CFFE+2A (= $D000 + 2 x sprite), sets or clears its $D010 bit and sets its $D015 bit. A is kept.

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00, active low): $FD = $FF up / 1 down / 0, $FE = $FF left / 1 right / 0, and $02 = 1 while fire is held. While the crash lock $0346 is non-zero the port is not read: no direction and no fire.

Shows the 16 world objects (live table $6900: 0 May Day, 1-14 police cars, 15 the bullet) on hardware sprites, object 15 down to 0. An object within the window (X - $0338 below $140, Y - $033A below $70) that is not shown gets its sprite (flags bits 0-2) if that sprite is free, else is marked waiting (bit 6); a shown one (bit 7) is placed with place_sprite at X offset + 7, Y offset + $90 with pointer $6920. A shown object that leaves the window loses its sprite (and multicolour); if flag bit 4 is set the object is reset from its template in $6800; the flags are cut back to the sprite number.

Object outside the window: a shown one has its sprite and multicolour bits cleared; then flag bit 4 selects a reset of all six coordinates from the template page $6800. Oddity: for a shown object the bit-4 test reads $6910,Y with Y = its sprite number, not the object's own flags.

Resets an object that left the window with flag bit 4 set: X, Y (low and high), shape and direction are copied back from its template in $6800-$68FF, so a shot police car reappears at its starting place.

A shown object leaving the window: its sprite's bits in $D015 and $D01C are cleared (masks $03C0), then the flags for the bit-4 test are read as $6910,Y with Y = the sprite number (see object_offscreen).
Cuts an object's flags back to its sprite number (bits 0-2) and goes on to the next object.

Hand-over entry, where the depacker jumps: sets the sound option $02E0 to 3 (theme and effects), points the BRK vector $0316 and the NMI vector $0318 at restart_to_menu ($43D0), so RESTORE goes back to the instruction page, writes $D0 into $0304 too (the low byte only of the BASIC tokeniser vector; why is unknown), clears irq_lock $02FF and jumps to title_page.

Stack reset stub: SEI, stack pointer $FF, CLD, then the instruction page (title_page, $4F30). The BRK and NMI target, and where world_update goes when a chase ends without a catch ($0313 = $40 or a damage count).
Stack reset stub for the good ending: SEI, stack pointer $FF, CLD, SID volume 0, then mission_complete ($5800). world_update jumps here when $0313 = $80 (May Day caught).
A third stack reset stub, byte for byte like restart_to_menu (jumps to $4F30). No jump, vector or table found names it; probably a spare.
Gunshot, if effects are on ($02E0 bit 1): voice 3 noise at frequency $FAAA, attack/decay $09, sustain/release 0, gate on.
Crash, if effects are on: voice 1 noise at frequency $04AA, attack/decay $1C, sustain/release $01, gate on. Used for roadblock hits and for a police car being shot.
Tyre screech for a handbrake-turn step, if effects are on: voice 3 control $61 (pulse and sawtooth, gate) at frequency $24AA, attack/decay $12; then back to world_update.

Called for each non-space character the success telex types: volume 15, $D417 = $0F, gate off, voice 1 frequency $3AAA, attack/decay $08, sustain/release $07, then control $61 (sawtooth and pulse, gate on): a short note for every letter, the telex's clatter.

Speed gauge: fills screen cells $0576-$057D with character 4, then writes character (delay / 2) AND 3 into cell $0576 + 7 - delay / 8 (delay = $0340), so the mark moves along the gauge with the speed; continues into draw_damage_gauge.

Damage gauge: damage $03A1 / 8 picks a screen cell up a column (damage_gauge_lo/hi: $0515, $04ED, $04C5, $049D, $0475, then $0475 three more times) and writes character $C4 + (damage AND 7) there, so the gauge rises an eighth of a cell per point; from 40 on, the top cell is drawn again.
Low bytes of the damage gauge's eight screen-cell entries, bottom to top: $0515, $04ED, $04C5, $049D, $0475, and $0475 three more times for damage 40 to 63.
High bytes of the damage gauge's eight entries (05, then 04 seven times).

Fires the car's gun unless sprite 6 (the bullet) is already on: object 15 goes to the car's world position plus ($AA, $31), flags $C6 (shown, sprite 6), pointer $AC, heading = the car's $03A0; plays gun_sound.

The first-person view through the windscreen, rebuilt when the map has moved a cell ($0336). The view point is the map window pointer $033C nudged one cell along the last coarse scroll (Y $0335 for headings with $6BD0 = 1, else X $0334), kept in $02FA/$02FB (never read). Reads the 33 cells named by the heading's offset list ($6D00 + $6B30[heading]) into $6B00-$6B20; the first cell with a non-zero attribute ($6F00) scanning $6B15 down to $6B0B gives the wall's type and depth (1-11, or 0 for none). Columns 9-0 come from cells $6B01-$6B0A and 12-21 from $6B17-$6B20: eight screen codes each from the cell type's strip ($6C00/$6C80) at 8 x a column number. The wall ahead comes from $6A00-$6AFF by type and depth. The 22 x 8 result lands in the buffer at $0D09 and $0337 tells copy_3d_view.

From the IRQ: when build_3d_view has finished a picture ($0337 non-zero), copies its 22 x 8 characters from the buffer at $0D09 (40-byte rows) to the screen at $0409 (rows 0-7, columns 9-30) and clears $0337.

Distance from the car to May Day for the locator: |object 0 X - $88 - car X $0338| + |object 0 Y - $32 - car Y $033A| (16 bits, via $EA-$ED), divided by 16 (divide_16_8); the quotient plus 1 becomes the beep interval $034D, which only the silent locator_beep reads.

Places a roadblock: site ($0399 AND $1F, the frame counter as the random choice) of roadblock_kind/_lo/_hi. Kind $48 fills three cells side by side, kind $49 three cells one above the other (126 apart), with that character.
Car against a roadblock: if the car's cell ($C9) holds a roadblock character ($48 or $49), the three cells around the new cell pointer $AE are cleared and damage is added; otherwise nothing.
Roadblock of kind $48: clears the cells at $AE, $AE+1 and $AE-1, then add_damage.
Roadblock of kind $49: clears the cells at $AE, $AE+126 and $AE-126, then add_damage.
Adds one to damage $03A1 for a roadblock; at 47 the chase ends ($0313 = 47); otherwise crash_sound.

Clears roadblock site X (0-31): writes 0 (open road) into the three cells place_roadblock would fill. init_game runs it for all 32, which also wipes the marker cells $1C-$1F the map holds at each site at the hand-over.
Copies the cockpit picture: 1000 screen codes from cockpit_screen ($8B28) to the screen at $0400 and 1000 colours from cockpit_colours ($8F10) to colour RAM $D800.

Locator lamp and beep: while the lamp (colour RAM $D803, row 0 column 3) is red, $034C counts down; at zero the lamp turns purple for two calls ($034E), $034C is reloaded from the interval $034D and voice 2 beeps (triangle, frequency $3A04, attack/decay $98, sustain/release $DF); when the lamp goes red again the gate is released. Its only caller is the dead tail of irq_sound ($51EF), so the lamp never blinks and the beep never sounds: no call in 30 seconds of a chase with sound option 3.

Unsigned division of Y:A (high:low) by X, eight quotient bits: quotient in $FD, remainder in $FE (non-restoring: subtracts or adds back the divisor by the last result's sign; uses $AE and $02). Correct only while the quotient fits in a byte.
The 32 roadblock sites, kind: $48 three cells side by side, $49 three cells one above the other (place_roadblock, clear_roadblock).
The 32 roadblock sites, low byte of the map address of each site's first cell.
The 32 roadblock sites, high byte of the map address of each site's first cell ($95-$CC).

Speech for the way the last chase ended, from the instruction page loop: $0313 = $80 (caught; only reachable after RESTORE on the success screen) plays sample $1225; $40 (altimeter reached 000) plays $190A; any other value (damage full) plays $1090 and then $190A. The sample address is poked into play_speech at $1002 (low) and $1006 (high). Then clears $0313 and resumes the loop at $4F7F.

Police cars, objects 14 down to 1, and the bullet's movement (object 15 only moves); world_update calls it every pass. A shown car hit by the bullet (its sprite bit in $02FC) goes to police_shot, a dying one (flag bit 5) to police_dying. A car stays idle until the pursuit counter $03A2 reaches its threshold ($69E0); a car named in $02FD (it touched the player or another car) has its countdown set to $20 and does not move. Otherwise its countdown $6950 runs down; when it expires it is reloaded from $6960 (4-7, the car's speed), the cell under the car is read ((Y/8) x 126 + X/8 + $9372, multiply_8_8), a junction marker $12-$19 there sets its heading to the marker AND 7, and it moves one pixel along its heading (dx $69B0, dy $69B8) with that heading's shape from $69A0. The bullet moves every pass.
Unsigned multiply A x X by shift-and-add: product high byte in A and $FE, low byte in X and $FD (uses $02).

A shot police car: every $18 passes ($6990) its blink count $6970 drops and the shape alternates $AD/$AE; when the count runs out its sprite and multicolour bits are cleared and its flags become sprite | $50 (waiting, reset from the template when next outside the window).
The bullet hit this police car: its sprite goes multicolour, $02FC is cleared, flags | $70 (dying, waiting, reset), blink count $6970 = 16, crash_sound.

The map cell under the car: pointer = $033C, moved by the last coarse scroll ($0335 by 126, $0334 by 1), plus $0308 (row 6, column 20 of the window). When the car has moved exactly one 3-cell block since the last call (-378, +3, +378, -3: up, right, down, left), the cell it left is examined: a junction marker $12-$19 is rewritten with the marker of the direction taken ($18, $12, $14, $16), and police_ai steers by those markers, so the police follow the car's route; any other cell except that direction's $1F/$1C/$1D/$1E adds one to the pursuit counter $03A2, and each time it reaches 20 a roadblock is placed (place_roadblock) and it drops to 18.
Low bytes of the four one-block moves car_cell_update recognises: -378 (up), +3 (right), +378 (down), -3 (left).
High bytes of the four one-block moves ($FE, $00, $01, $FF).
The junction marker written for the direction the car left a junction by: $18 up, $12 right, $14 down, $16 left (police_ai takes marker AND 7 as a heading: 0, 2, 4, 6).
Per direction, the one cell value that does not raise the pursuit counter when left that way: $1F up, $1C right, $1D down, $1E left.

Chooses May Day's landing point: a random number from the SID (sid_random), bits 0-2, picks one of eight entries; target X from $4FC0/$4FC8 and Y from $4FD0/$4FD8 go to $69FC-$69FF, the spiral limit from $4FE0 to $D3.

The instruction page and its loop. Sets irq_lock $02FF to $98, text mode with character set $3000, sprites off, SID volume 0, clears the crash lock $0346, switches off CIA 1's interrupts ($DC0D = $7F, read to clear) and draws the page (show_title_page); the IRQ vector is left as it is, and no interrupt runs on the page. Loop: read_joystick; fire jumps to $FCE2, the KERNAL's reset entry, which finds the CBM80 signature at $8004 and enters the game through the cold-start vector at $8000 (= game_start, $5A00); stick down/up steps the sound option $02E0 between 1 and 3; a delay of $50 x $FF loops; the title colour $D9 steps; the page is redrawn (redraw_title_page). A non-zero $0313 (result of the last chase) sends it to speak_result first.
May Day's eight landing points, X low byte (pick_landing_point).
Landing points, X high byte (0-3).
Landing points, Y low byte.
Landing points, Y high byte (0-2).
Landing points, the spiral limit copied to $D3 ($F0-$FC): how wide she circles before homing.
Random byte: voice 3 set to noise at frequency $FFFF with the gate off; returns the oscillator output $D41B in A.
Points the IRQ vector $0314 at game_irq ($5026), sets the raster compare to line $8B (bit 8 cleared) and enables the raster interrupt in $D01A.

The chase's interrupt handler (entered through the KERNAL, which has pushed A, X and Y). A raster interrupt goes to raster_bands. Any other is ignored while irq_lock $02FF is set; otherwise a sprite-background collision goes to hit_background, a sprite-sprite collision to hit_sprite, and anything else plays the theme (music_tick, $5046). No such third kind was seen: $5046 had no hit in 30 seconds of a chase.

Acknowledges the raster interrupt and splits the screen by the current line: below $8F raster_map_band, below $9C raster_map_colours, otherwise (line $FB, bottom of the map) this part: collision interrupts off, next compare $8D, Y scroll 3 with 25 rows, X scroll 0 with 40 columns, background light grey, multicolours 8 and 9, character set $3000 for the cockpit; then the frame's work: copy_3d_view, irq_sound, and, with interrupts allowed again (CLI), car_move_tick and update_clock.

Raster line $8B/$8D, just above the map: background, multicolours and sprite multicolours blue, next compare $9A, character set $3800, the map's fine scroll (Y from $033F, X from $033E; the Y value also clears $D011 bit 3, 24 rows), sprites 0-3 and 6 blue.

Raster line $9A, the map's colours: background dark grey, multicolours yellow and green, sprite multicolours red and yellow, sprite 0 light red, 1 light grey, 2 white, 3 and 6 black; next compare $FB, and the sprite-background and sprite-sprite collision interrupts are switched on for the map band.

Sprite-sprite collision ($D01E). Anything involving sprites 4-5 (the steering wheel) is ignored. May Day's sprite 3 with the car's sprite 7 ends the chase as caught ($0313 = $80), but only once the catch flag $02E1 is set (altimeter below 060). Sprite 7 with a police car goes to car_hits_police. Sprite 6 (the bullet) with police sprites stores them in $02FC and stops the bullet; other collisions among sprites 0-2 go to $02FD.
Sprite-background collision ($D01F): the car (sprite 7) hitting scenery is a crash (car_crash); the bullet (sprite 6) hitting scenery stops it (bullet_stop).
Stops the bullet: object 15's X and Y high bytes ($694F, $69CF) become $FF, so the next objects_to_sprites finds it outside the window and frees sprite 6.
Interrupt exit: pulls Y, X and A as the KERNAL pushed them, RTI.

The car (sprite 7) touched a police car: police sprites 0-2 not in multicolour (not already shot) are stored in $02FD, which makes those cars wait, and the crash is handled (car_crash); if any of them is multicolour (already shot) the collision is ignored.

The car hits a building (hit_background) or a police car: ignored while the crash lock $0346 is set; otherwise the gear flips ($03A4 EOR 8, so the car bounces back the way it came), the move delay grows by 3 (at most $3F), damage $03A1 grows by one (at 40 the chase ends with $0313 = $27), the crash lock is set (read_joystick ignores the stick until scroll_map next moves the car) and the heading returns to $0347, that of the last move.
Sound, once a frame, called by raster_bands: the theme (music_tick) when $02E0 bit 0 is set (options 1 and 3), then RTS.

Never runs: the rest of a locator beep call, cut off by the RTS at $51E9, which sits where LDA $02E0's opcode would be. The bytes decode as CPX #$02 (the LDA's operand), LSR, BEQ, JSR locator_beep, JMP irq_exit. This is locator_beep's only caller.

May Day's parachute (object 0), while $0313 is 0. Before homing ($02FE = 0), every 7th call: one pixel along her drift direction $6930 (dx/dy tables $69B0/$69B8), shape from $03E0; when the countdown $69F8 runs out the radius $69F9 grows by 2 and the direction turns one step anticlockwise, so she circles outwards; when the radius equals the spiral limit $D3 homing starts. Homing (every 8th call, mayday_homing): one pixel in X and in Y towards the landing point $69FC-$69FF. Then altimeter_tick.

Circling phase of mayday_update: reload the countdown with 7, move object 0 one pixel along drift direction $6930 (dx $69B0, dy $69B8), set her shape from $03E0, and on each expiry of $69F8 widen the radius $69F9 by 2 (homing starts when it equals $D3) and turn the drift direction one step anticlockwise.

Homing phase of mayday_update: reload the step countdown with 8 and move object 0 one pixel towards the target X ($69FC/$69FD) and one towards the target Y ($69FE/$69FF), stopping in each axis when equal.

Every 21st call ($535C) counts the altimeter, screen $04F3-$04F5 (digits $64-$6D), down by one. Once it reads below 060 the catch flag $02E1 is set; at 000 $0313 = $40: May Day has landed before the car reached her.
Countdown byte (20 calls) inside the code area, used only by altimeter_tick.

Sound option highlight: sets the colours of the three option lines ($53FD-$53FF) to green ($05), the one chosen by $02E0 (1 theme only, 2 effects only, 3 both) to light green ($0D), then draws the page (draw_title_text).
Colour RAM values for the instruction page's three sound-option lines at $53FD-$53FF (green $05, the chosen one light green $0D, indexed by the option 1-3); $53FC itself is only the index-0 slot.
Colour of the THEME TUNE ONLY line (option 1), set by highlight_option.
Colour of the SOUND EFFECTS ONLY line (option 2), set by highlight_option.
Colour of the BOTH line (option 3), set by highlight_option.
Fills screen $0400-$07E7 with the space code $15 and colour RAM $D800-$DBE7 with light blue $0E (four pages from $03E8/$D7E8 with Y starting at $18).
One JMP to highlight_option: the title loop's per-pass redraw of the instruction page.

Draws the sixteen 40-character lines of the instruction page (title_text, $5500-$577F) to screen rows 1, 4-8, 12, 14-19 and 21-23 with their colour RAM: row 1 in the stepping colour $D9 (the flashing PRESS FIRE TO START), the story red, JOYSTICK CONTROLS yellow, the controls light blue and the three sound options from $53FD-$53FF.
Clears the screen (clear_screen), then colours and draws the instruction page (highlight_option).
Instruction page text, line 1 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "PRESS FIRE TO START".
Instruction page text, line 2 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "MAYDAY HAS JUMPED FROM THE EIFFEL".
Instruction page text, line 3 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "TOWER AND IS NOW PARACHUTING TO".
Instruction page text, line 4 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "HER DROP POINT. FOLLOW HER AND GET".
Instruction page text, line 5 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "THERE FIRST! WATCH OUT FOR THE".
Instruction page text, line 6 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "POLICE AND ROAD BLOCKS.".
Instruction page text, line 7 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "JOYSTICK CONTROLS".
Instruction page text, line 8 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "FORWARD ACCELERATE".
Instruction page text, line 9 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "BACKWARD REVERSE BRAKE".
Instruction page text, line 10 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "LEFT STEER LEFT".
Instruction page text, line 11 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "RIGHT STEER RIGHT".
Instruction page text, line 12 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "FIRE SHOOT".
Instruction page text, line 13 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "REUERSE+FIRE HANDBRAKE TURN".
Instruction page text, line 14 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "THEME TUNE ONLY".
Instruction page text, line 15 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "SOUND EFFECTS ONLY".
Instruction page text, line 16 of 16 (40 codes, $80-$99 = A-Z, $15 space): "BOTH".

The good ending: sets irq_lock $02FF, text mode with character set $3000, sprites off, clear_screen, speech sample $1225 (interrupts stay off from there), then the ten lines of the telex at $8028 are typed onto rows 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 19 (tables $5880/$5890) by type_line, each letter with a type_click, and it stops in the endless JMP at $5879. The City Hall code in the telex, CCPHJ, is fixed text: nothing computes it.
High bytes of the screen rows the ten telex lines are typed on (mission_complete).
Types one 40-character line from ($FB) to ($FD), with a delay of about $3F x $FF loops after each character; a non-space character calls type_click, a space writes 0 to voice 1's control register.
type_line's per-character pause: saves X and Y, counts $3F x $FF, restores them and moves to the next of the 40 characters.

The chase begins here, entered through the KERNAL reset: fire on the instruction page jumps to $FCE2, which sees CBM80 at $8004 and jumps through $8000. Runs init_game, init_music, draw_cockpit, install_game_irq, pick_landing_point a second time (init_game has already run it once) and car_draw, clears irq_lock $02FF, then falls into main_loop.

The chase's main loop, free-running (not synchronised to the raster). Every pass runs world_update ($5A66). Counter $0344 (16) sends every 16th pass through speed_and_fire first; counter $0345 (2) makes every second of those a steering pass too: read_joystick and steer_car ($5A60), which continue into speed_and_fire.
main_loop's counter stores: the not-yet pass goes straight to world_update, the 16th pass to speed_and_fire.
main_loop's steering pass: read_joystick, then steer_car.

One pass of the world: objects_to_sprites, draw_speed_gauge (and the damage gauge), build_3d_view, mayday_distance, mayday_update, police_ai, car_cell_update, roadblock_check. Then the end test on $0313: 0 loops to main_loop, $80 goes to restart_to_success, any other value to restart_to_menu.
The stick's left/right value at the last steering pass (car_draw), to tell a fresh push from a held one.
Held-stick allowance: 1 when the stick was centred on a straight heading, 0 on a diagonal; a held stick turns while it stays non-negative.
Steps left in a handbrake turn (4 at the start, one 45-degree step per steering pass).
The heading the handbrake turn has reached so far.

Steering, every 32nd main-loop pass. A handbrake turn in progress ($5AA2 non-zero) turns the car one step anticlockwise per call from $5AA3; on the last of its four steps the reverse flag $03A4 is cleared and the car's heading $03A0 takes the new direction; the sprite is redrawn and screech_sound played. Otherwise the stick's left/right ($FE) turns the heading $03A0 (0 = up, then clockwise, 8 directions) one step: a fresh push turns at once, a held stick turns again only while $5AA1 allows, so holding it stops at the next straight heading.

Stick steering in steer_car: centred stick clears steer_last and sets steer_hold from the heading's parity; a held stick spends steer_hold; a push turns the heading one step (right +1, left -1, wrapping 0-7) and redraws the car.

Remembers the stick's left/right value in $5AA0 and draws the map car as sprite 7 at the fixed screen position X $AB, Y $BD with the pointer for its heading from $03A8 ($80-$87); falls into speed_and_fire.

Speed, gear and fire, every 16th main-loop pass. While the stick is pushed sideways the two steering-wheel sprites swap shapes ($07FD toggles $A1/$A3, $07FC = one less). Forward gear: stick up lowers the move delay $0340 (faster, not below 1), down raises it, and at $40 the gear flips to reverse ($03A4 = 8, delay $3F); in reverse down speeds up and up slows down and flips back. Fire starts a handbrake turn (four steps, $5AA2 = 4, from the current heading) when in reverse with a delay below $15 and no turn running; otherwise fire shoots (fire_bullet).

Moves the car two pixels along its heading (index $03A0 OR $03A4: reverse uses entries 8-15) by scrolling the map under the fixed car sprite. X: table $0370 (0, 1, or $81 = negative) steps the fine scroll $033E by 2 and the car's world X $0338 by 2 the other way, flagging a coarse step (bit 0 of $03A7) when the fine scroll wraps; Y likewise with $0380, $033F, $033A and bit 1. Clears $0341 and the crash lock $0346. On a coarse step (map_coarse_step) the map moves a whole cell and is redrawn.

A whole-cell scroll: the map window pointer $033C moves by the heading's cell step ($0350: 1 column, $0360: $7E, one row; negative entries move back), $0334/$0335 record the last X/Y step (-1, 0, 1), then the 13 rows of 40 cells are copied from the 126-cell-wide map to screen rows 12-24 ($05E0-$07E7), the copy's source and destination operands at $5D6C-$5D71 being advanced row by row; $03A7 is cleared and $0336 asks for a new 3D view.
Operand of LDA abs,Y in the map-window copy: the map address of the current row minus one, set from $033C and advanced by $7E per row.
High byte of the map_copy_src operand, carried into by the row step.
Operand of STA abs,Y in the map-window copy: the screen address of the current row minus one, starting at $05DF (row 12) and advanced by 40 per row.
High byte of the map_copy_dst operand, carried into by the row step.
Tail of the map-window copy: after each 40-cell row the source operand advances by $7E (one map row) and the destination by 40 (one screen row), 13 rows in all (X from $0D).

Car movement clock, once a frame from the IRQ: counts $0342 down; when it passes zero it is reloaded with the move delay $0340 / 4, the heading is saved in $0347 and scroll_map moves the car two pixels, so the car moves every delay/4 + 1 frames. Skipped while irq_lock $02FF is set.

3D view column graphics, 8 screen codes per column at 8 x the column number: the strips for map cell types at $6000 (types 4, 6, 8, $0E-$11, $1B), $60B0 (0, $12-$1A, $1C-$1F) and $6160 (2, 9-$0D, $20-$23), per cell_strip_lo/hi; the depth-0 wall piece at $6100 lies inside the $60B0 strip.

3D view graphics $6200-$65FF: the wall-ahead pieces for wall type 0 at depths 1-11 ($6210, $6220, $6240, $6270, $62B0, $6300, $6360, $63D0, $6450, $64E0, $6580; wall_ptr_lo/hi), each 8 codes per column it covers.

3D view graphics $6600-$67FF: the end of the nearest type-0 wall piece, the strip at $6630 for cell types 1, 3, 5 and 7, and at $66E0-$67FF more columns of the same form that no pointer found reaches.
Object templates, copied to the live table $6900 by init_game (object 0 May Day, 1-14 police cars, 15 the bullet): X low byte. init_game first sets object 0's X and Y here to $01FA.
Object templates: flags; bits 0-2 the sprite (May Day 3, police 0-2, bullet 6), bit 4 reset from template when off screen, bit 5 dying, bit 6 waiting for its sprite, bit 7 shown.
Object templates: sprite pointer (May Day $90, police $8A-$8E, bullet $AC).
Object templates: heading 0-7 (May Day's drift direction, a police car's heading).
Object templates: X high byte.
Object templates: police step countdown (1 each).
Object templates: police step reload, passes per pixel (3-7; lower is faster).
Object templates: blink count of a shot car (0; set to 16 by police_shot).
Object templates: Y low byte.
Object templates: blink timer of a shot car ($0A; reloaded with $18 by police_dying).
Police car sprite pointers for headings 0-7: $88-$8F (shapes $2200-$23FF); $68A8-$68AF, a near copy (88-8E, 00), are not read.
X step per heading 0-7 for police cars, the bullet and May Day: 0, 1, or $81 (one back).
Y step per heading 0-7: $81 (up), 1 (down) or 0.
Object templates: Y high byte.
Sixteen bytes of the template page ($68D0-$68DF, copied to $69D0) that nothing found reads.
Object templates: the pursuit count ($03A2) a police car waits for before it moves (1 for all fourteen).
Template tail: $68F0-$68F7 unread; $68F8/$68F9 May Day's spiral countdown and radius (1, 0); $68FC-$68FF her landing target, overwritten by pick_landing_point.
Wall-ahead pieces for build_3d_view, index = wall type (0, or $10 for cell attribute $90) + depth 0-11: low byte of the piece's column graphics ($6100-$65FF for type 0, $7000-$73FF for type $10).
Wall-ahead pieces: high byte of the column graphics pointer ($61-$65, $70-$73).
Wall-ahead pieces: first column (10 down to 0 as the wall comes nearer).
Wall-ahead pieces: column after the last (12 up to 22), so a near wall fills the whole view.
Offset of each heading's cell list in view_offsets: 0, 0, $42, $42, $84, $84, $C6, $C6 (one list per pair of headings).
$6B38-$6BCF: stale copies of wall-table rows and fill bytes; nothing found reads them.
Per heading: 1 when build_3d_view nudges its view point by the last Y scroll (headings 2, 3, 6, 7), 0 when by X.
$6BD8-$6BFF: another stale copy of wall-table rows; not read.
Per map cell type 0-$23: low byte of its 3D column graphics (build_3d_view adds 8 x the column); $6C24-$6C7F zero.
Per map cell type 0-$23: high byte of its 3D column graphics ($60, $61 or $66); $6CA4-$6CFF zero.

The cells in view, as 16-bit offsets from the view base (view point - $05D6): four lists of 33 words, for headings 0-1 ($6D00), 2-3 ($6D42), 4-5 ($6D84) and 6-7 ($6DC6), read by build_3d_view into $6B00-$6B20.
view_offsets, the lists for headings 4-5 ($6D84) and 6-7 ($6DC6, to $6E07).
$6E08-$6EFF after the offset lists: zeros, then $84 fill from $6EB0; not read.

Attribute of each map character for build_3d_view: $80 a building (a solid column; the first one ahead also sets the wall type 0), $90 for characters 2 and 4 (wall type $10), 0 for open ground (characters 0, $12-$1A, $1C-$1F, $F0-$FF).

3D view graphics $7000-$73FF: wall-ahead pieces for wall type $10 (cell attribute $90, characters 2 and 4) at depths 1-11 ($7000, $7010, $7030, $7060, $70A0, $70F0, $7150, $71C0, $7240, $72D0, $7370).
The last 32 codes ($DD) of the nearest type-$10 wall piece, which runs from $7370 to $741F.
Per-voice attack/decay for the theme ($09, $19, $1A), set by init_music.
Voice 2's attack/decay ($19).
Voice 3's attack/decay ($1A).
Per-voice waveform control ($81 noise, $21 sawtooth, $41 pulse).
Voice 2's waveform ($21 sawtooth).
Voice 3's waveform ($41 pulse).
Per-voice pulse width high byte ($00, $0E, $06).
Voice 2's pulse width high ($0E).
Voice 3's pulse width high ($06).
Flips between 0 and 1 after each note step (music_tick). Both of music_tick's paths wait for three frames, so it changes nothing.
Frames since the last note step.
Per-voice note stream pointer, low bytes ($7A23-$7A25).
Voice 2's stream pointer, low byte.
Voice 3's stream pointer, low byte.
Per-voice note stream pointer, high bytes ($7A26-$7A28).
Voice 2's stream pointer, high byte.
Voice 3's stream pointer, high byte.
Per-voice frames left in the current note ($7A29-$7A2B).
Voice 2's frames left in its note.
Voice 3's frames left in its note.
Per-voice frequency low byte of the current note, the base for music_pitch_fx ($7A2C-$7A2E).

Theme tune setup: per-voice attack/decay ($09, $19, $1A), waveform ($81 noise, $21 sawtooth, $41 pulse) and pulse width high byte ($00, $0E, $06) into $7A18-$7A20; filter cutoff $09/$73, $D417 = $05 (voices 1 and 3 through the filter), $D418 = $3F (volume 15, low- and band-pass); then music_rewind.
Points the three voices' note streams at $E000, $EAD1 and $F755 ($7A23-$7A28) and sets each note countdown ($7A29-$7A2B) to 8. Also the loop point when voice 1 reaches the end of its stream.

Theme tune, once a frame when chosen: music_pitch_fx, then the frame counter $7A22 steps the notes (music_step_voices) on every third frame (about 16.7 steps a second on PAL), whichever value $7A21 holds, since both paths compare with 3; music_rewind restarts the tune when voice 1's stream pointer reaches $EAD1.
For voices 0-2: copies the voice's stream pointer into $D9/$DA and its attack/decay, waveform, pulse and countdown into $7A30-$7A33, runs music_voice_note, and stores the pointer and countdown back.

One voice: counts its note length down; at zero starts the next note: gate off, attack/decay, frequency high and low from the stream (the low byte also kept in $7A2C+voice), pulse width high, waveform with gate on, and the new length; notes are three bytes (frequency high, frequency low, length), read with music_read.
Reads byte Y of the current note at ($D9) with $01 = 0 (all RAM), because the tune lies in the RAM under the KERNAL at $E000-$FFFF, then restores $01.
Per-frame pitch effects: voice 1's frequency low byte climbs by $0A each frame (a rising noise), and voices 2 and 3 get 0, 4, 8, 12 in turn added to their note's low byte (a fast shimmer).
SID register offsets of the three voices: 0, 7, 14.
